issues.description: The problem statement requires public constructors that accept all attributes in the order shown in the UML (for Ride: name:String then abbreviation:char). In the solution, Ride only defines a constructor Ride(String name) and sets abbreviation to a default, which does not match the required constructor signature and order. This contradicts the specification and will confuse students about the expected constructor signature for Ride.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the Ride class to provide a public constructor that accepts both attributes in the UML order: Ride(String name, char abbreviation). Alternatively, if the educational intent is to provide a default abbreviation, explicitly document that deviation in the problem statement. Prefer changing the Ride constructor to Ride(String name, char abbreviation) to match the UML and tasks.

issues.description: The solution repository contains an internal inconsistency: RollerCoaster and subclasses (e.g., LaunchedRollerCoaster, LaunchedDropdownTower) call super(name, abbreviation) but the Ride class in the solution does not define a matching constructor. This makes the solution code uncompilable and contradicts the intended inheritance/constructor chaining described in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Ride constructor signature match the expectations of subclasses by adding Ride(String name, char abbreviation). Ensure RollerCoaster and other subclasses call an existing super(...) constructor with the same parameter types and order. Alternatively, adjust subclass constructors and super(...) calls to match the Ride constructor, but the former (adding the two-parameter Ride constructor) is preferable to align with the UML and problem requirements.
